# Preface {.unnumbered}

TODO(prose): why this book, who it is for, what it assumes. The short version: this is the
engine-room companion to *Social Network Analysis*. That book says what to compute and why. This one
says how it gets computed, quickly and correctly.

## Who this book is for {.unnumbered}

TODO(prose): people who use graph libraries and want to know what is underneath, analysts who hit a
network too big for their tools, and students meeting graph algorithms for the first time. No
computer science degree assumed; every idea starts from a tiny example you can check by hand.

## How the book is organized {.unnumbered}

The book has ten parts: foundations, traversal and paths, structure, flow and matching, centrality at
scale, communities, generating and sampling graphs, layout and embedding, scale and engineering, and
case studies. Each chapter opens with what it assumes and closes with exercises and a summary.

## Code, for now {.unnumbered}

The code in this book is still being written. Every spot where code will go holds a stub that names
what it will do, so you can see what is coming.
